episodes.174684: A strong Pacific storm system brought isolated high winds and isolated flooding from heavy rain.
episodes.175023: Pacific trough draws two atmospheric rivers, November 8-9, 2022.
episodes.175218: An anomalously low upper level trough brought widespread snow to the region. Wet snow fell in the Ada County area, causing traffic delays and widespread damage due to falling branches and trees from accumulating wet snow on foliage.
episodes.175329: A storm system brought heavy snow to the Sierra Nevada and southern Cascades. Reports of 15 to 44 inches of new snow were received in the northern Sierra, with heavy snow reported down to around 3000 feet in the southern Cascades. Northbound Interstate 5 was closed 10 miles north of Fawndale for approximately 5 hours on the night of the 7th and again for about 4 hours on the 8th due to winter weather conditions. During the event, chain controls were in place on Interstate 5, Interstate 80, US Highway 50 and other mountain highways. A brief EF-0 tornado was confirmed 4 miles north northwest of Galt on the morning of the 8th, with minor damage reported.
episodes.175864: Hurricane Nicole made landfall near Vero Beach, Florida as a Category 1 Hurricane on Thursday, November 10, 2023 with estimated maximum sustained winds of 75 mph. The system was originally classified as a subtropical storm after forming several hundred miles east of the Bahamas before it gained tropical characteristics as it approached Grand Bahama and Abaco Island. The interplay between Nicole and an expansive area of high pressure over the eastern United States produced a large wind field of tropical storm force over the western Atlantic, with a long northeast fetch that stretched over 1000 miles. These onshore winds generated very large seas in excess of 30 feet offshore, which over multiple unusually high tide cycles, led to moderate to severe beach erosion across east central Florida. Damage to coastal structures was extensive, particularly across Volusia County where an already weakened shoreline due to Hurricane Ian succumbed to the long-duration high surf event. Two indirect storm-related fatalities were reported in Orange County.

events.narrative: Heavy rain fell across the San Bernardino County Mountains on November 8. The following are rain reports from the region:|Mesonet station FW6602 Running Springs reported 5.11 inches of heavy rain.|Mesonet station SSVC1 San Sevaine Lookout reported 3.66 inch of heavy rain.|Mesonet station LTLC1 Lytle Creek RAWS reported 3.12 inch of heavy rain.
A rainfall total of 0.74 inches was measured at CoCoRaHS station ID-AD-46 in Boise.

Heavy rain fell across Orange County on November 8, leading to flooding. The Department of Highways reported flooding on the off ramp of I-5 at El Toro Rd near Lake Forest, and flooding on the onramp to I-5 from Oso Parkway.

Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding at SR-60 West and the Phillips Ranch Road offramp in the morning, with an additional report of two vehicles stuck in flood waters after attempting to drive through a closed off ramp onto Euclid.

Ontario Fire department reported 6 person in the swiftwater channel in John Galvin park where the channel begins near I-10. Rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches per hour had occurred from 7 am to 9 am in Ontario and Rancho Cucamonga. 3 persons were rescued. 3 more person were later found drowned in a retaining pond which was filled 15 to 20 feet high with storm runoff water. The bodies were not found until several days later due the water being too deep and low visibility. Multiple agencies were involved in the week long recovery efforts. The channel runs south past Ontario airport to where it reached the storage collection ponds on East Philadelphia Street. Search and rescue in Cucamonga Channel reported by CalOES and Ontario Fire Department. As many as 10 people experiencing homelessness were swept away as a surge of water occurred following 2 hours of heavy rain. Five people were immediately rescued, one person immediately reported deceased, with two additional bodies recovered (one of November 14, the other on November 16).

Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding at I-10 W/Euclid Ave, with three lanes experiencing water and debris. The offramp of Highway 91 to Adams street was also flooded.

Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches which fell between 0700EST on the 8th and 1500EST on the 10th led to generally nuisance type to minor street flooding across portions of Lake County. The St. Johns River at Astor, which was already in moderate flood stage due to the remnant effects of Hurricane Ian, experienced water level rises as early as the 8th due to increasing north to northeast winds impeding the river's flow. Renewed flooding was reported along numerous streets and communities along the river in Astor. At Deland, already in minor flood stage, river gauges recorded a rise into moderate flood stage on the 9th. A damage assessment provided by the county indicated a total of 44 residential and manufactured homes were affected in the area at a cost of approximately $1.4M.

Rainfall totals of 3-6 inches, which fell between 0700EST on the 8th and 1500EST on the 10th led to generally nuisance type to minor street flooding across portions of Volusia County. The St. Johns River at Astor, which was already in moderate flood stage due to the remnant effects of Hurricane Ian, experienced water level rises as early as the 8th due to increasing north to northeast winds impeding the river's flow. Renewed flooding was reported along numerous streets and communities along the river in Astor. At Deland, already in minor flood stage, river gauges recorded a rise into moderate flood stage on the 9th.

Rainfall totals of 4-7 inches, which fell between 0700EST on the 8th and 1500EST on the 10th, led to generally minor street flooding across portions of the county. The St. Johns River at Sanford, which was already in minor flood stage due to remnant effects from Ian, experienced water level rises to moderate flood stage on Thu. Nov. 10. Above Lake Harney at Geneva, the river, which was already in minor flood stage, experienced slow rises into moderate flood stage in the days after. A small number of structures experienced at least some damage according to reports; however, official estimates were unavailable at the time of this writing.

Heavy rain fell across the San Bernardino County Mountains into the far northern portions of the Inland Empire on November 8. The Department of Highways reported that SR-18 was closed in both directions due to flooding from 48th street to SR-138/18 bridge, as well as water flowing over the roadway on Institution Road and Verdemont Ranch Road.
A rainfall total of 0.74 inches was reported by a member of the public one mile northeast of Boise.

Heavy rain fell in and around the Apple/ El Dorado burn scar on November 8, resulting in debris flow and flash flooding. Roadway flooding was reported on Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road, with the roadway washing out at 12099 Oak Glen Road.
A rainfall total of 0.74 inches was measured by CoCoRaHS station ID-AD-21.
Department of Highways reported washouts on Ice House Canyon Road and Mt Baldy Road, with vehicles stuck. Total rainfall of 3.7 inches at Mt Baldy.

The Department of Highways reported flooding and debris on Highway 138 and Waters Drive, with 3 inches of water covering the roadway. Total rainfall of 3 to 4.5 inches at Crestline to Lake Arrowhead. Mud and debris also covered Cajon Blvd and Kenwood Ave.

Periods of moderate rainfall fell across the San Diego metro area on the afternoon of November 8. Several reports of flooding were received:|The Department of Highways reported flooding on Highway 94 and Federal Blvd, where 0.50 inch fell in three hours.|The Department of Highways also reported flooding at SR 94 and College Ave.|A National Weather Service employee reported roadway flooding on University Ave where rainfall of 0.25-0.30 inch had been reported in one hour.

Heavy rain fell in and around the Apple/ El Dorado burn scar on November 8, resulting in debris flow flooding. Roadway flooding was reported on Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road at 12099 Oak Glen Road. El Dorado burn scar and flood prone area has had many prior flash floods and debris flows.
Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding in one lane on SR-79 at Garboni Road.
Chollita Rd was flooded.
Sunnyslope Dr was flooded.

Swiftwater rescue along North Indain Canyon Drive in Whitewater Wash in Palm Springs around 12:30 PM. Multiple vehicles were trapped with three drivers and a dog rescued successfully. Multiple roads, including Gene Autry Trail, Indian Canyon Drive, Vista Chino Road and North Indian Canyon Drive remained closed through 6 AM the following day.

A weak tornado touched down near Highway 99 and Arno Rd., about 4 miles NNW of Galt. The California Highway Patrol reported a tin roof from a barn blown off and downed powerlines over Arno Rd. and a bus had windows blown out. Maximum estimated wind speeds were 70 mph. Path length was approximately 0.8 miles, path width 400 yards,  |from preliminary information.

Department of Highways reported flooding at the intersection of Arrowhead Lake Road and Havenhurst Road.
